title: Immediate Effects of Active Prisms on Reading Automaticity and Motor Control in Young Adults With Developmental Dyslexia
official: Effet d'Une Modification de l'état Initial du système Dynamique Sur Les capacités d'Automatisation de Jeunes Adultes Dyslexiques
summary: Developmental dyslexia is associated with persistent difficulties in reading automaticity. AUTO-DYS investigates whether a single, brief intervention using active prisms changes the complexity of nonlinear movement dynamics and reading automaticity in young adults with dyslexia. This single-center, prospective, non-randomized controlled study will enroll 66 adults aged 18-30 years: 33 with developmental dyslexia and 33 typical readers. All participants will undergo reading, postural-control, and working-memory assessments before and after an experimental period during one visit. Only participants with dyslexia will receive individually selected active prisms; typical readers will repeat the assessments without active prisms. The main hypothesis is that modifying tonic muscle distribution with active prisms is associated with increased dynamic complexity and improved reading automaticity in participants with dyslexia.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Adults aged 18-30 years with normal or corrected vision.

Dyslexia group: documented medical diagnosis of developmental dyslexia and an Alouette-R C index greater than two standard deviations, as specified in the protocol, on the study day.

Control group: typical readers with an Alouette-R C index less than two standard deviations, as specified in the protocol, on the study day. Eligibility will be verified by the study physician.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Optical correction exceeding ±0.75 diopters
* known balance or psychiatric disorder
* another diagnosed neurodevelopmental disorder in the dyslexia group
* any diagnosed neurodevelopmental disorder or proprioceptive dysfunction in the control group
* pregnancy
* legal guardianship
* pathological near-vision Parinaud test (P2)
* refusal of consent.
